I graded `submissions/s2.json` and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. You got 3 correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Correct | The model only writes a request that names the tool and its arguments. |
| q3 | Wrong (M6) | You picked "it will eventually fix the bug". It sees the same failure every step, so more steps add nothing. It needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. |
| q4 | Partial (M4) | 4 is right. Your reason, that the model runs the tools itself, is wrong. The model requests a tool and the program runs it. |
| q5 | Correct | You gave both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide its next step. |
| q6 | Partial | The name is only part of it. The model chooses from the full tool description: name, purpose and parameters. |

**What to work on next:**
- Write a description for `check_calendar` with its name, what it does and its parameters.
- Add one sentence saying who runs the tool and what the model outputs.
- That covers the q4 and q6 gaps and is the skill your mission needs.

I also added learning record `0003-model-requests-program-runs.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. `s1` is still ungraded.
